ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast bimodal distribution; dominant high-intensity white pixels (approx. 65%) across lateral lobes with low-intensity black pixels (approx. 35%) concentrated at the median base, trailing edges, and tips.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central bifurcated low-intensity region extending from the base towards the mid-lobes; high-intensity white contiguous zones on the left and right lobes; dense low-intensity stippling and solid banding along the distal trailing edges and outer tips.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central indentation; calculated internal angle approximately 65 degrees with a significant vertical depth relative to the horizontal lobe span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular pixel-level serrations along the entire trailing boundary; notable deep irregular notches on the inner margin of the left lobe and smaller rhythmic peaks across the right lobe trailing edge.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetrical upward convexity on the distal margins, tapering to sharp, slightly recurved tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized low-intensity pixel clusters concentrated at the outer tips and along the trailing edge margins; no distinct circular clusters visible within the central white zones.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, vertical low-intensity linear disruptions (rake marks) observed on the right lobe's high-intensity surface and a singular diagonal mark on the lower left lobe near the base.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant irregular tissue loss or deep notches on the inner trailing edge of the left lobe; multiple vertical linear abrasions on the right lobe surface.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly distinctive dark 'butterfly' or 'inverted Y' pigmentation pattern originating at the median notch and radiating towards the center of each lobe.
